chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'For the one who prays the Prayer of Jaʿfar, is recorded for him in reward the like of what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Jaʿfar.' He said: 'Yes, by Allah.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِي وَ اللَّهِ: Yes, by Allah, an affirmation of truth
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)
key_terms.صَلَاةَ جَعْفَرٍ: The Prayer of Ja'far, a specific recommended prayer in Shia tradition

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying Salat al-Ja'far according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the high spiritual status of Ṣalāt Jaʿfar by linking its reward directly to the Prophet’s commendation of Jaʿfar ibn Abi Ṭālib, thereby emphasizing the intergenerational transmission of merit within the Ahl al-Bayt. The Imam’s affirmation ('I swear by Allah') underscores the authenticity and significance of this specific prayer form, which is widely practiced in Shia tradition for seeking needs and expressing gratitude.
